title: The 5 Tallest Waterfalls on Earth, Ranked (Niagara Isn't Even Close)

scenes.text: The five tallest waterfalls on Earth, ranked. Niagara isn't close, and number one is nearly a kilometer tall.

scenes.label: Yumbilla · 896 m
scenes.text: Number five: Yumbilla Falls in Peru. About eight hundred and ninety-six meters tall, and still the shortest on this list.

scenes.label: Olo'upena · 900 m
scenes.text: Number four: Olo'upena Falls in Hawaii. About nine hundred meters, and the only American waterfall in the top five.

scenes.label: Tres Hermanas · 914 m
scenes.text: Number three: Tres Hermanas Falls, also in Peru. About nine hundred and fourteen meters of falling water.

scenes.label: Tugela · 947 m
scenes.text: Number two: Tugela Falls in South Africa. About nine hundred and forty-seven meters, only thirty-two short of number one.

scenes.label: Angel Falls · 979 m
scenes.text: Number one: Angel Falls in Venezuela. Nine hundred and seventy-nine meters in total, almost a kilometer. Nothing on Earth falls farther.

description:
The five tallest waterfalls on Earth, ranked by total height.
From Yumbilla in Peru to Angel Falls in Venezuela, which is almost a kilometer tall.
Which of these would you most want to stand under?
first_comment: Which waterfall would you visit first? And what should we rank next?
